title: Linux_P2P_Ransom_Botnet_Investigation_1c9
description: Investigate and respond to a Linux P2P Ransom botnet incident.
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service management
Usage of netstat for network diagnostics
Identifying systemd timers for persistence mechanisms

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential security incidents. Your task is to investigate and respond to these incidents. Learning objective: Identify and mitigate a Linux P2P Ransom botnet, a type of peer-to-peer malware that encrypts files and demands a ransom for decryption.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication. The flag type is a service name.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for any unusual or unauthorized services that might be communicating externally. The suspicious service is likely the bot-beacon.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services using the command: systemctl list-units --type=service

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system configuration and are communicating with external hosts. Use the command: systemctl status <service-name> to check the status and external communication of each service.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic. The flag type is a service name.

**Question:** What is the name of the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and look for services that are generating excessive traffic. The service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic is likely the bot-flood.service.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate network connections using the command: netstat -tuln

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use tools like netstat or ss to identify services with high network activity. Look for services with high packet counts or unusual destinations. Use the command: netstat -tulnp | grep <service-name> to check the network activity of each service.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot. The flag type is a timer name.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Check systemd timers and services to identify how the service is automatically started. The persistence mechanism is likely the system-update-checker.timer.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd timers using the command: systemctl list-timers

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd timers and services that are not part of the standard system configuration. Use the command: systemctl cat <timer-name> to inspect the configuration of each timer.
